evidence: add-address.usecase.ts: when canMutateResource fails it returns ErrorFactory.UseCaseError(`User with id ${userId} not found`, null, HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)

delete-address.usecase.ts, set-default-address.usecase.ts and update-address.usecase.ts: when canMutateResource fails they return ErrorFactory.UseCaseError(`User with id ${userId} not found`) without HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND

When the user is missing: add-address returns 'User not found' with NOT_FOUND, delete-address returns 'User not found' with no status, and set-default-address and update-address return `User with id ${userId} not found` with no status

Input types: AddAddressUseCase uses AddAddressCommand and UpdateAddressUseCase uses UpdateAddressCommand (both from ../../../commands), while delete-address.usecase.ts declares its own DeleteAddressInput and set-default-address.usecase.ts declares its own SetDefaultAddressInput
Failure checks: add and update use isFailure(userResult); delete and set-default use userResult.isFailure
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four use cases share one concern: changing a user's addresses through the User aggregate. Each one loads with userRepository.findByIdForUpdate, calls an aggregate method, then calls save. That part is consistent. However, two rules are copied into all four use cases, and the copies differ. (1) Each file repeats the rule that a failed ownership check is reported as 'not found'. Only the add use case passes HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND; the other three use the ErrorFactory default. Callers therefore get different HTTP behaviour for the same failure. (2) The same is true of the 'user not found' handling after loading the user. The message also differs: 'User not found' in add and delete, versus `User with id ${userId} not found` in set-default and update. In addition, the input types are defined two ways. Add and update take command classes from application/commands. Delete and set-default each declare their own input interface inside the use-case file. The code also checks for failure two ways: isFailure(userResult) in some places and userResult.isFailure in others. Because these checks are copied instead of kept in one place, the unit fails the rubric.

violations.message: The 'not found' handling for a failed ownership check and a missing user is copied here, and it differs from the other use cases: this file passes HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND explicitly and the others don't. This rule should live in one shared place.

This file declares its own DeleteAddressInput instead of using the command classes that the sibling use cases use. It also repeats the ownership and missing-user checks without the NOT_FOUND status and with the message 'User not found'.
This file declares its own SetDefaultAddressInput instead of using a command class. It also repeats the ownership and missing-user checks, and its handling differs from the add use case.
This file repeats the ownership and missing-user checks but leaves out the HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND that the add use case passes.
